originalTitle: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop that blocked takeoffs for hours
summary: Takeoffs from airports throughout the US largely stopped on Friday after the FAA issued a national ground stop at 3:44PM ET "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." content: Takeoffs from airports throughout the US largely stopped on Friday after the FAA issued a national ground stop at 3:44PM ET “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” More than four hours after the stop was issued, officials announced it was lifted at 8:15PM ET and that flights will resume. It’s unclear how many flights will be able to take off and when, as they now face problems of overloaded airports and flight crews that have run out of time to operate the planes, meaning many people will be stuck where they are for the time being and more flights will be delayed or canceled. In a White House press conference announcing that the stop had been lifted, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed an aging air traffic control system that he is pursuing funds to replace, saying that the TRACONs (Terminal Radar Approach Control) in the air traffic control centers “started to have inconsistency in the data from the radars and the communications from airplanes.” He said that the devices that had the issue were analog telecom devices, where the switches / routers “got overloaded with data” and started to show inconsistency. An earlier report from CBS News cited multiple sources who said that an update to the air traffic control system’s private communications network, operated by L3Harris, caused a system reboot and the subsequent outage. L3Harris has not yet responded to a request for comment from The Verge, but during the press conference, Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed that “patches” to the existing system sparked the issue. In response to a reporter’s question about the patches and how they contributed to the outage, Duffy said, “By doing nothing, you inject way more risk into the system… I didn’t anticipate that we would have an outage like this.” [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6-jBdt7kU-w] The flight tracking site FlightAware lists 9,124 US flights as delayed and 5,901 flights canceled as of 8:39PM ET. According to CNN, the last nationwide ground stop in 2023 lasted for about 90 minutes after the NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) system for pilots went down, and the last one prior to that was after the attacks on September 11th, 2001. Speaking to reporters outside the White House on Friday afternoon, Mullin told reporters that there is currently no reason to suspect a cyberattack or other national security threat, or any connection to the recent Microsoft Outlook outage, but that at the time no cause had been ruled out for the “telecommunications outage.” [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hz1cNNgtLtM] When asked about any possible connection to the cloud-based AI Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) system that was activated nationwide on November 10th, he said they were looking into that. Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company that designed the system and was awarded a 12-year $875 million contract in June to deploy it, denied any connection, tweeting “The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC.” Jon Ostrower of The Air Current reports that the outage began with the Chicago air traffic control center, followed by centers in Boston, Washington, New York, and Minneapolis, and as the FAA issued a ground stop for aircraft flying east, more facilities began reporting problems. He said the problems disrupted both the radar and radio frequencies used by air traffic controllers and pilots. [Media: https://twitter.com/AirSpaceIntel/status/2121371183836696583] Updated, Friday, November 13th: Added that the stop has been lifted, and quotes from the press conference.
chineseTitle: 美国联邦航空局取消了导致起飞数小时受阻的全国范围内的地面停车
chineseSummary: 美国东部时间下午 3:44，“由于特殊情况和安全原因”，美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 发布全国地面停飞令后，美国各地机场的起飞基本上于周五停止。发布禁令四个多小时后，官员们宣布于东部时间晚上 8:15 解除禁令，航班将恢复。目前尚不清楚如何[...]
chineseContent: 美国东部时间下午 3:44，“由于特殊情况和安全原因”，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 发布全国地面停飞令后，美国各地机场的起飞基本上于周五停止。发布禁令四个多小时后，官员们宣布于东部时间晚上 8:15 解除禁令，航班将恢复。目前还不清楚有多少航班能够起飞以及何时起飞，因为他们现在面临机场超载和机组人员没有时间操作飞机的问题，这意味着许多人将暂时被困在原地，更多的航班将被延误或取消。在宣布取消禁令的白宫新闻发布会上，交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 指责空中交通管制系统老化，他正在寻求资金更换该系统，并表示空中交通管制中心的 TRACON（终端雷达进场控制）“雷达数据和飞机通信开始出现不一致”。他说，出现问题的设备是模拟电信设备，其中交换机/路由器“数据过载”并开始显示不一致。哥伦比亚广播公司新闻早些时候的一篇报道援引多个消息来源称，L3Harris 运营的空中交通管制系统专用通信网络的更新导致系统重启和随后的中断。 L3Harris 尚未回应 The Verge 的置评请求，但在新闻发布会上，Duffy 和国土安全部部长 Markwayne Mullin 证实，现有系统的“补丁”引发了该问题。在回答记者有关补丁以及它们如何导致中断的问题时，达菲说：“如果不采取任何行动，就会给系统注入更多风险……我没有预料到我们会发生这样的情况。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
